note: The first De Franceschi families this archive has been able to document in Carnia itself — the country the family says it came from, and where every account of its origin has until now been tradition rather than record.

mione.claim: In 1679 a list of village headmen recorded, at Mione: «Zuane De Franceschi con un suo fiolo, Zuane d'Erman: questi tre nell'Istria, luogo imperiale» — a De Franceschi of Mione with a son, working in Istria, in the imperial place. Carlo De Franceschi, writing about 1873, said the family had come from Carnia and settled in Istria «intorno al 1700», and that De Franceschi were still living at Mione and Muina in his own day.
mione.found: They still were in 1939. Monsignor Lucio Soravito de Franceschi was born at Mione di Ovaro on 8 December 1939, ordained priest in 1963, professor of pastoral theology at the Udine seminary from 1977 and at the Faculty of Theology of Northern Italy from 1991, archpriest of Udine cathedral from 1999, and Bishop of Adria-Rovigo from 2004 to 2015. He died on 6 July 2019.
mione.why: Soravito is a Carnian house-name — soravìt, «above Vito's» — of the kind that fuses onto a surname to tell one branch of a village family from another. A Soravito de Franceschi at Mione is a De Franceschi of Mione with the house attached. Two hundred and sixty years after the headmen's list, the name is still in the village.

paluzza.what: The earliest of them. Zuanne is the Venetian form of Giovanni — the same name the 1679 list gives the man of Mione.

paluzza.with: Maria Silverio, daughter of Gasparo Silverio and Orsola Moser

paluzza.what: Daughter of Daniele and Maria Silverio.
Their sons Francesco, born 14 December 1807 at Naunina in Paluzza, and Pietro Antonio, born 5 June 1810.
Their son Pietro, born 1851 at Paluzza, married Maria Lazzaro — and dead at forty-four in the civic hospital at San Daniele del Friuli on 30 March 1895, entered in the register as a mason.
Their daughter Maria, born 1865 at Paluzza.
